headline: High: Aider can write and modify a shared git repo while the paired list-only ML resource offers no isolation, creating prompt-injection, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a git repo, so malicious content in repo files could influence its instructions. The paired awesome-production-machine-learning profile is a non-runnable list with no ingestion surface, so direct bidirectional injection is limited; uncertainty about any external wrapper means I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped by another tool that reads repo files as instructions, injection risk increases.
IF agent_a processes untrusted repository content as prompts, file-based instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Separate instruction files from data files in the repo.
Require explicit human review for any file Aider is asked to edit.
Use a branch-per-task workflow with protected main.
Add a prompt-injection lint step for repo text.
requires-engineering: sandbox Aider in a throwaway clone with no shared working tree.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, but the paired awesome-production-machine-learning profile is non-runnable and has no data classes or egress. That makes cross-agent leakage from B implausible; the main exposure is A's own provider calls, not a pairwise leak.
conditions: IF agent_b is replaced with a runnable agent that reads the same workspace, leakage risk rises.
IF source code or git history contains secrets, Aider may transmit them to its configured provider.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before use.
Use a local-only model provider for Aider.
Restrict Aider to a scrubbed branch.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning pre-commit hooks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has read/write filesystem access, shell execution, and modify_git_state, while the paired awesome-production-machine-learning profile is non-runnable and has no writes. The conflict is therefore mostly one-sided, but shared git-repo state in Aider can still collide with other instances or wrappers; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF another writer modifies the same git repo concurrently, commit conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b is embedded in a workflow that mutates the same workspace, write contention becomes real.
mitigations: Use one writer per branch.
Lock the repo during Aider sessions.
Stash or commit before switching tasks.
Keep generated artifacts out of tracked paths.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. The paired awesome-production-machine-learning profile is only a curated list, so it is not itself an action-taking agent; still, if its content is used to steer Aider without verification, errors can cascade into bad commits.
conditions: IF Aider's generated edits are auto-merged without review, incorrect changes can propagate.
IF the list content is used as a source of truth for code or config decisions, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require code review before merge.
Diff-check Aider commits against the task spec.
Pin any referenced guidance to a vetted source.
Add tests before accepting edits.
requires-engineering: enforce CI gates on Aider-authored commits.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history and may send prompts to configured model providers, so compliance concerns center on code residency and secret handling. The paired awesome-production-machine-learning profile is a public, non-runnable list with no data classes or retention policy, so there is no second-agent residency mismatch to cite.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the repo, Aider may move it to external model providers.
IF the repo contains secrets or personal data, retention and residency obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the repo.
Use a provider with an approved DPA.
Redact secrets before prompting Aider.
Set short retention on provider logs.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls.
